marks.selector: canvas, svg path.line, svg path[class*='line'], svg path[class*='city'], svg path[class*='row'], svg path[class*='col'], svg g:not([class*='axis']) > path
marks.note: lines are Canvas paths or SVG paths. Class-contains matchers cover common naming variants; svg g:not([class*='axis']) > path catches unclassed data paths inside non-axis groups (e.g. Claude output). Max raised to 600 because bg+fg layers each produce ~150 paths.

axes.note: class-contains matcher removed: g[class*='axis'] also matches 'axis-brush' and 'axis-title' groups, inflating the count. Named-class alternatives cover observed variants. 2026-09-25 (d3-power-tools): outermost=true counts only matches with no matching ancestor, so a g.axis inside a g.axis-group counts once (it counted 12 for 6 axes).

rows.note: 6 data rows (one per axis) plus optional header / footer

brush.note: drag on the brush group itself; the selection rect inside is initially zero-size and not directly clickable

notes: Tracer-bullet fingerprint. Selectors are intentionally permissive (CSS contains-class matchers) since model implementations vary.
The harness exercises brush by simulating a drag on the first axis's brush group; effect is asserted via DOM diff (count-badge text changes; table sparkline DOM nodes change).

Calibrated post-first-run: marks band widened to 50–300 (d3.line and d3.curve generate extra control-point paths beyond the literal row count); table.rows max=10 (header + footer common); count_badge selector accepts #count id. Brush trigger is the brush group itself rather than the inner selection rect (which is zero-size before user interaction).
